A Pulmonary Allergy Drugs Advisory Committee (PADAC) meeting was held on June 23, 2011.

recommendation.text: The panel voted 12 Yes, 1 No in favor of approval for marketing of icatibant; it also voted that the efficacy data were sufficient (12 Yes, 1 No), that the safety data were adequate (11 Yes, 1 No, 1 Abstain), and expressed near-unanimous support for patient self-administration (11 Yes, 1 No, 1 Abstain).

quote.quote: The panel voted 12 yes, 1 no that the data supported approval for marketing of icatibant.

summary: A Pulmonary-Allergy Drugs Advisory Committee (PADAC) meeting was held on June 23, 2011, during the Complete Response review cycle (an earlier PADAC meeting had been cancelled in the original cycle because efficacy was not demonstrated). The committee was broadly supportive, voting 12 Yes / 1 No in favor of approval, 12 Yes / 1 No that efficacy was sufficient, 11 Yes / 1 No / 1 Abstain that safety was adequate, and 11 Yes / 1 No / 1 Abstain in support of patient self-administration. The review documents record concerns (blinding adequacy, use of a median time point to summarize efficacy, generalizability to subgroups such as ethnic minorities/obese/pregnant/cardiac patients) and a suggestion by several members to develop a postmarketing registry, but none of the review documents tie any of these concerns to a resulting change in the approval: the only postmarketing requirements in the approval letter are rat/mouse carcinogenicity studies and impurity characterization (driven by Pharmacology/Toxicology findings, not the AC), no REMS was imposed, and the registry the members referenced (the Icatibant Outcome Survey) was already an ongoing voluntary program before the meeting. No supported concern-to-change linkage was found.
